newsitem.title: USA: Hearing set on Sacramento, Calif., $80 mln arena.
newsitem.headline: Hearing set on Sacramento, Calif., $80 mln arena.

text.p: A June 9 hearing has been set in Superior Court to decide if Sacramento can proceed with the sale of up to $80 million of notes to refinance a basketball arena, according to a report on Monday.
Judge John Stroud has asked the city and opponents of the arena deal to submit briefs on Wednesday ahead of the hearing, the Sacramento Bee newspaper reported.

In April, the city of Sacramento asked the court to "validate" the note sale. City attorneys said the validation process would clear away the legal challenges facing the deal and allow the city to quickly issue the notes.
The Sacramento City Council approved the note plan in February in a bid to keep the National Basketball Association Kings playing in the city.
With the proceeds of the note sale, the city would refinance $51.5 million of Arco Arena debt, where the Kings play. The remaining note proceeds would be used to refinance other franchise debts.
The notes were expected to be sold in April. But the deal was put on hold after at least two lawsuits were filed against the city's proposal.
If the Superior Court judge validates the deal, attorneys for the city said they would ask the court to dismiss the lawsuits.
